key_insight: An incremental Deep Energy Method can model ductile fracture by coupling history-dependent J2 plasticity with a phase-field fracture formulation and separate neural representations for displacement and damage.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a meshless, energy-based alternative for predicting crack initiation and growth in elasto-plastic solids with results close to finite-element references.
method: Minimize a reduced total energy alternately for displacement and phase-field fields.
Use a ReZero residual network for displacement and trainable localized Gaussian RBFs for the phase field.
Update plasticity locally with radial return and carry constitutive history across load steps via transfer learning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with finite-element reference solutions for force-displacement response, energy evolution, plastic deformation, and crack propagation.
watch_item: Accuracy becomes more sensitive to load-step size near abrupt fracture events, so incremental control is important.
paper_title: A deep energy method formulation for phase-field modelling of ductile fracture
